reuse.why: The flag is threaded through the existing assertBankAccountNotLinked guard, and the unlink field-clearing is pulled out of unlinkAccount into clearAccountLink, which both paths now use.

duplication.why: The unlink field reset is shared through one new helper instead of being copied. The six provider changes are just one-line parameter passes.

placement.why: The unlinking side effect lives inside a function named and used as an assertion, so a guard now changes data, and it does so before the new link is made.

scope.why: The change touches only the link parameters, the guard, the extracted helper and one test.

maintainability.why: It is small and reuses the unlink semantics, but a mutating 'assert' with a boolean parameter will surprise future readers. Renaming it or moving the takeover into its own step would fix that.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Uses assertBankAccountNotLinked and the unlink field reset (now clearAccountLink) rather than going around them.

disguised_duplication.where: The unlink update block is moved into clearAccountLink and called from unlinkAccount, not reshaped and copied.
